title: Infosys Opens 330,000-Square-Foot Indore Block for AI and Cloud Work
excerpt: The SDB-2 building at the Super Corridor campus, inaugurated on September 16, expands the center's capacity in AI, cloud, and cybersecurity; the Indore site now employs more than 3,300 people.
body:
• Infosys inaugurated SDB-2, a 330,000-square-foot Software Development Block, at its Indore Development Center in the Super Corridor on September 16, 2026.
  • The expansion adds delivery capacity in cloud, application development, AI and machine learning, and cybersecurity; the Indore center now employs more than 3,300 people serving global clients across BFSI, retail, life sciences, and manufacturing.
  • Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav led the inauguration alongside Infosys CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka, signaling state support for central India's technology push.
  • The company will deepen academic partnerships with IIT Indore, IIM Indore, and Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya; the new block follows high-performance green building standards.

Bengaluru — Infosys has inaugurated a 330,000-square-foot Software Development Block at its Indore Development Center, adding delivery capacity for artificial intelligence, cloud, and cybersecurity work in central India. The SDB-2 building, located at the company's Super Corridor campus, was inaugurated on September 16, 2026, the company announced.

The Indore center currently employs more than 3,300 people supporting global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, life sciences, and manufacturing. The expanded facility will strengthen Infosys' capabilities in cloud, application development, AI and machine learning, and cybersecurity to address evolving client requirements.

The inauguration ceremony was led by Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, with Indore Member of Parliament Shankar Lalwani and MLA Manoj Nirbhay Singh Patel in attendance. Infosys was represented by Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka, Executive Vice President Sunil Kumar Dhareshwar, and Senior Vice President Niladri Prasad Mishra.

Context & background

Infosys has been steadily building its presence outside India's largest metros, and the Indore expansion continues that push into tier-2 delivery hubs. The Super Corridor has attracted IT parks and corporate campuses as companies seek lower operating costs and access to regional talent. The new block deepens Infosys' footprint in Madhya Pradesh, where the company says it plans to tap central India's growing technology talent pool.

https://x.com/Infosys/status/2100258618582986943

The expansion is framed around the company's "AI-first" positioning. Infosys, which employs more than 325,000 people across 59 countries, has been reorganizing its service lines around AI-assisted delivery, cloud transformation, and cybersecurity as enterprise clients shift spending toward those areas. A new block dedicated to those capabilities in Indore gives the company added delivery scale at a time when Indian IT majors are competing on both cost and specialized AI talent.

The Madhya Pradesh government has been courting IT investment with incentives and infrastructure around Indore, which it pitches as an alternative to Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune. Yadav's presence at the inauguration underscores that pitch — and the state's expectation of jobs in return.

"Indore is steadily emerging as an important technology hub, supported by a strong talent base and a growing innovation ecosystem. Infosys' investment in Indore will create employment opportunities for the state's skilled youth and further strengthen Madhya Pradesh's technology ecosystem."

— Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh

Impact & analysis

For Infosys, the Indore expansion adds scale in a cost-efficient location while the industry recalibrates. Indian IT services growth has been uneven, with clients scrutinizing discretionary spending but continuing to fund AI, cloud migration, and cybersecurity projects. A new dedicated block focused on those four areas signals where Infosys expects demand to concentrate over the coming years.

The talent dimension is equally important. Rather than drawing solely from saturated metro markets, Infosys plans to deepen its engagement with Madhya Pradesh's academic and technology ecosystem through skilling programs and institutional partnerships with IIT Indore, IIM Indore, and Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya. That pipeline gives the company early access to engineering graduates while anchoring its hiring story in the region.

"We are delighted to expand our presence in Indore, reflecting our ongoing investment in talent, innovation, and digital capabilities. The expansion will enable us to leverage the region's strong talent pool, strengthen our capabilities across AI, cloud, and digital technologies, and deliver greater value to our global clients."

— Jayesh Sanghrajka, Chief Financial Officer, Infosys

What's next

The new building is aligned with Infosys' ESG commitments and high-performance green building standards. It is designed to be environmentally friendly and energy efficient, incorporating low-energy cooling, smart building automation, rainwater harvesting, and wastewater recycling. The facility will also house flexible workstations, training facilities, and wellness centers, according to the company.

Staffing numbers for the new block and the specific client programs that will run out of Indore have not been disclosed. What is clear is the trajectory: Infosys is doubling down on regional delivery hubs and academic-linked hiring, a model that could serve as a template for further expansion in central and eastern India as the company chases its AI-first ambitions. The Hindu BusinessLine reported the inauguration on September 16.
